tossups.text: The Tisza (TEE-suh), the longest tributary of this river, flows through the Pannonian Basin. The Iron Gates are a gorge on this river that form part of the border between Serbia and Romania. The capital of Hungary was formed from a merger of two cities separated by this river. This river is the longest river in non-Russian Europe. Budapest and Vienna lie on, for 10 points, what Central European river that drains into the Black Sea?

The first biography of this leader was written by the Italian diplomat Daniele Varè, who gathered his sources while he was stationed in Beijing. A plot to murder this leader was concocted by a philosopher who wrote a utopian treatise which outlined a scheme to mass-marry Chinese and Europeans to breed a master race, called the Da Tongshu. This leader's reputation suffered badly from the smear campaign that followed, orchestrated by Liang Qichao ("l'yang chee-chao") and the aforementioned Kang Youwei ("yoh-way"). This leader instigated a set of reformist "New Policies" at the urging of Yuan Shikai ("y'wen shu-kye"), despite having arrested the Guangxu ("gwong-shoo") emperor and purged most promoters of the Hundred Days Reform a few years prior. After that palace coup, this leader encouraged anti-European sentiment among the Harmonious Fists. For 10 points, name this Boxer Rebellion enthusiast who ruled as Empress Dowager during the late Qing dynasty.

A solution of picroindigo carmine is used to visualize these cells on a "Christmas tree" stain. Swellings called hydroceles ("hydro-seals") and hematoceles ("hemato-seals") can interfere with the storage of these cells, which are found in a pouch of serous membrane called the tunica vaginalis. These cells initiate membrane fusion upon binding to (emphasize) another class of cells' ZP3 receptors. An influx of calcium ions into these cells through the CatSper channel initiates capacitation. The anterior side of these cells contains an acidic vacuole called the acrosome that secretes hydrolytic enzymes to break down a different cell's zona pellucida ("pel-LOO-sid-uh"). These haploid cells develop in the seminiferous tubules and are stored in the epididymis ("epi-DID-uh-miss") before traveling through the fallopian tubes. For 10 points, name these male gametes that fertilize eggs.

In a novel, producers of this good form a union at the urging of Lester Mead, but the title "Strong Wind" breaks the movement. In another novel, a man who produced this good is thrown onto an ocean-bound train filled with a bunch of corpses, but when people do not believe his tale about his ordeal, he spends the rest of his days studying alchemy. Miguel Asturias ("ahs-TOO-ree-as") fictionalized the plight of workers producing this product in a trilogy named for it. Mr. Brown oversees producers of this good, and later has nearly all of those workers gunned down in a massacre described by José Arcadio Segundo in the novel One Hundred Years of Solitude. The nickname "El Pulpo" refers to a company that harvested, for 10 points, what fruit?

According to Apollodorus, he dishonored Hera every chance he got. He was so named because a mare stepped on his face and discolored it. This man killed his mother's stepmother at an altar of Hera. During his reign he allowed his half-brother to kill himself by drinking bull's blood but he killed his infant son Promachos. This son of Tyro and slayer of Sidero was the brother to Neleus. After his death, he was succeeded by his son Acastus. During the Olympics, this man was honoring his father Poseidon when he noticed a man with only one sandal, prompting him to issue a quest. For 10 points, name this king of Iolcus who sent Jason to get the golden fleece.

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for bone development and growth. It plays a key role in the musculoskeletal system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this skull-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The skull is a key component of the Musculoskeletal system, involved in bone development and growth.

tossups.text: Yann Weymouth designed a museum named for this man that includes works from the collection of Reynolds and Eleanor Morse. In a photo named for and containing this man, three cats and a bucket of water appear suspended in mid-air. That photo of this man by Philippe Halsman includes his painting Leda Atomica. A museum dedicated to this man is in St. Petersburg, Florida and is home to his work The Hallucinogenic Toreador. Another painting by this man includes swarming ants and melting clocks. For 10 points, name this Spanish artist of the surrealist painting The Persistence of Memory.
acceptableAnswers: Salvador Domingo Felipe Jacinto Dali i Domenech

tossups.text: this structure is essential for axial skeleton bones. It plays a key role in the musculoskeletal system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this skull-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The skull is a key component of the Musculoskeletal system, involved in axial skeleton bones.

tossups.text: One of his characters is annoyed when his girlfriend slips a gift of tobacco into his pocket, and appears in the same novel as Philip Ravelston, who edits the newspaper The Anarchist and is loosely modeled on the author's friend Richard Rees. That character is the best friend of Gordon Comstock, the author of London Pleasures and protagonist of Keep the Aspidistra Flying. In a similar autobiographical work, the author escapes hunger by remembering the deposit on lamp fuel and works in a French hotel in Down and Out in London and Paris. His time in India, Burma, and Spain is recounted in the autobiographical works Burmese Days, and Homage to Catalonia. For 10 points, name this English author best known for portraying the nation of Oceania and its ruling party, Ingsoc, in 1984.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for coronary arteries. It plays a key role in the cardiovascular system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this atrium-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The atrium is a key component of the Cardiovascular system, involved in coronary arteries.

tossups.text: This husband of Katherina von Bora was inspired to monastic life by a nearby lightning strike, and his followers included the Schmalkaldic League. Granted safe passage from Wartburg Castle by Frederick of Saxony, he argued at the Marburg Colloquy with Ulrich Zwingli about the Eucharist. This speaker at the Diet of Worms was irked by the sale of indulgences in Wittenberg. For 10 points, name this author of the 95 Theses, who started the Protestant Reformation.

This man abandoned his parents' religious beliefs after attending a 1922 Christian Student Conference in Peking. One of this man's patients was "Mrs. L" and her son, Jim, who destroyed a clay figurine that represented his father. While lecturing at the University of Rochester, he wrote The Clinical Treatment of the Problem Child. This man noted that a "growing openness to experience" and "increasing organismic trust" were characteristics of the "fully functioning person." His most famous theory stated that the professional should give empathy and unconditional positive regard to patients, encouraging them to develop their own solutions to a problem and was introduced in On Becoming A Person. For 10 points, name this psychologist who pioneered client-centered therapy.

The second Friedmann equation is sometimes named for this quantity and relates it to density plus three times the pressure. This quantity and charge are both squared in the numerator of the Larmor formula. A type of this quantity named for Fermi is experienced by a particle trapped between two magnetic mirrors. This quantity is the second derivative of position and the first derivative of velocity with respect to time. For 10 points, name this quantity measured in meters per second squared that appears in Newton's second law, and is equal to force divided by mass.

Along with Hephaestus, this deity was honored in the Chalceia festival, in which women wove a sacred peplos-depicting this deity's defeat of the giant Enceladus during the Gigantomachy-to honor her as the patron of handicrafts. After the fall of Troy, Cassandra embraced a statue of this goddess and begged for protection before being abducted by Ajax the Lesser. In one myth, this goddess overshadowed Poseidon's gift of a salt spring with her gift of the first domesticated olive tree. With that gift, she won the patronage of a city that later honored her by building the Parthenon. For 10 points, name this Greek goddess of the military and wisdom, the patron of Athens.

This ruler brought back his country's traditional religion after it was changed to a monotheistic one-deity religion by his father Akhenaten. Studies of this ruler's injuries have led to theories that he died in a chariot accident. This ruler's tomb in the Valley of the Kings supposedly cursed Lord Carnarvon and was found by archaeologist Howard Carter. For 10 points, name this "Boy Pharaoh" of Egypt who died at age 19.

Arun Auditto led the capture of Anjediva outside this colony, the smaller of two colonies where Casimiro Monteiro roused anti-independence interests. Khoja Zufar attempted to besiege a city in this colony, which Timoji helped conquer from the Adil Shahi dynasty. This colony's districts of Dadra and Nagar Haveli essentially declared independence in 1954, presaging a conflict in which this colony's cities of Daman and Diu were captured. Colony state, which was seized in Operation Vijay, is where Francis Xavier proselytized and is buried. Alfonso de Albuquerque established this colony by capturing its territory from the Bijapur Sultanate, which would begin 450 years of rule until its annexation by Jawaharlal Nehru. For 10 points, Portugal ruled what Indian state?

The translator's preface to Swami Vivekananda's version of this book claims that it echoes the theme of the Bhagavad Gita. In one chapter, this book references Job's assertion that "the life of man upon earth is a warfare" in warning against temptation, which it argues "steels the just" like fire tempers iron. This book contains an aphorism that is often translated as "man proposes, God disposes." This book's fourth section begins with an invitation to consume bread and wine, and its third section takes the form of a dialogue between the reader and the title figure. This book takes its title from its first section, which advocates despising all vanities on earth and contains the quote "how quickly passes the glory of the world." Four sections, including "Directives for the Interior Life" and "Helpful Counsels of the Spiritual Life," make up this book, which was written by a member of the Devotio Moderna movement in the 1400s. For 10 points, name this Catholic devotional by Thomas à Kempis.

These molecules are used in conjunction with sulfur hexafluoride in tracer-derived age measurements of ocean water. One member of this class of molecules can be synthesized by reacting chloroform with hydrofluoric acid, and in another important reaction these molecules can undergo photo-induced scission of their C-Cl bond to yield a long-living chlorine free radical. The most common member of this class of molecules is Freon-12, which was widely used in refrigeration until being phased out under the Montreal Protocol. For 10 points, name this class of halide-containing organic compounds used in aerosols which were largely responsible for the depletion of the ozone layer.

The feminist Sylvia Pankhurst is buried in Holy Trinity Cathedral in this city. Taxis known as "blue donkeys" provide transportation in this city, and it is served by Lideta and Bole airports. Attractions include Shango hall, which was built in before being transported there, and the eucalyptus trees that line the main streets. A statue known as "The Lion of Judah" stands in the middle of downtown in this city, which serves as the headquarters for the UN in . Situated at the foot of , this is, For 10 points, what city founded by Emperor Menelik II, the capital of ?

This anatomical structure, studied extensively in clinical medicine, this structure is essential for pharynx divisions. It plays a key role in the respiratory system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this pharynx-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The pharynx is a key component of the Respiratory system, involved in pharynx divisions.

parts.text: Its tributaries include the Rio Negro and the Purus, and accounts for one fifth of the world's total river flow. It is also the longest river on its continent, ahead of the Parana.

This river, along with its tributaries such as the Inkisi, has the second-largest flow in the world behind the Amazon. It names the two countries on its shores with capitals as Kinshasa and Brazzaville.

Just behind the Congo in terms of flow, this river originates in Lake Itasca and has tributaries such as the Rock and the Skunk rivers that meet this river at the Quad Cities and Burlington, Iowa, respectively.

bonuses.leadin: Identify these gigantic rivers from description, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Identify this Mexican reformer who became president of Mexico in 1911 after defeating Porfirio Diaz.

Madero's downfall came as the result of a coup by this man, supported by U.S. ambassador Henry Lane Wilson. The "tragic ten days" elapsed before this man assumed power, during which Madero was apprehended and killed.
Huerta himself did not last long, as this incident, in which Mexican soldiers temporarily imprisoned some American sailors, gave Woodrow Wilson a pretext for invading Veracruz and ousting Huerta.

bonuses.leadin: Emiliano Zapata broke with this man over land redistribution and issued his Plan of Ayala. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this deceptive term used for a group of illnesses including anemia and fatigue that inspired numerous documentaries on so-called "medical apartheid" and "medical racism."

None of the men treated for "bad blood" in the Tuskegee Syphilis Study received this antibiotic that became standard treatment for it. This antibiotic derived from fungus was discovered by Alexander Fleming.
Albert Bertheim and this German scientist were the first to synthesize arsphenamine. This scientist developed a staining method using methylene blue.

This British author of Mrs. Dalloway also wrote the novel Orlando inspired by their lover Vita Sackville-West.
Description acceptable. Woolf created this character to explain why women are disadvantaged in writing. While her brother can succeed, this character dies in London after becoming pregnant.

parts.text: This god was suckled by the goat Amalthea and suspended from a tree by the nymph Adamanthea during his time on Mount Ida. His mother Rhea had given birth to him in a cave on Crete in order to hide him from his father Cronus.
This group of figures, who are often conflated with the Phrygian Korybantes and the Lemnian Cabeiri, danced and banged their spears on their shields during Zeus's birth to drown out his cries.
This decad of demigods was born when Rhea dug her hands into the earth during labor. Three Phrygian ones named Acmon, Damnameneus, and Celmis are said to have invented the art of iron-forging.

parts.text: Name this city. Ludwig Mies van der Rohe designed an iconic leather chair for a pavilion that he and Lilly Reich designed for this city. A curvy, modernist building in this city is sometimes called "the stone quarry".

This photographer spent several days photographing a man cleaning the Barcelona Pavilion for one of his many "near documentary" photographs. This contemporary Canadian photographer has produced photographic recreations of works like A Sudden Gust of Wind by Hokusai or A Bar at the Folies Bergere by Monet.
The Barcelona Pavilion was built for the 1929 edition of one of these events. The Crystal Palace was built for the first of these events, which took place in London in 1851.

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with sweat glands.
What is the main function of the hair follicle in the integumentary system?
Name another component of the integumentary system related to sweat glands.

parts.text: Name this story in which Baptista Trewthen marries Charles Stow right before an arranged marriage to Mr. Heddegan, only to go ahead with the arranged marriage when Charles drowns an hour after the wedding.
The author of "A Mere Interlude" also wrote this novel in which the title character has the child "Little Father Time" with Arabella Donn and later marries his cousin Sue Bridehead.
"A Mere Interlude" and Jude the Obscure were written by this author who wrote about the rise and fall of Michael Henchard in The Mayor of Casterbridge.

bonuses.leadin: The protagonist of this story gets married because she hates her job teaching, but is dismayed to find that her husband only married her because he wanted her to teach his daughters for free. For 10 points each:

What is the main function of the colon in the digestive system?
Name another component of the digestive system related to colon sections.

parts.text: Name this quantity, the amount of money owed by the U.S. government. The limit, or "ceiling," on this quantity must be periodically raised by Congress to allow the government to continue paying off this quantity.
If the debt ceiling crisis is not averted, the government would fail to pay its debts on time, a situation named this. A bankruptcy court may supervise people if they do this on their loans.

The #mintthecoin movement urges this current Secretary of the Treasury to avoid default by minting a trillion-dollar platinum coin and deposit it with the Federal Reserve. This woman served as chair of the Fed from 2014 to 2018.

bonuses.leadin: The hashtag #mintthecoin [mint the coin] gained popularity as Republicans refused to increase this quantity. For 10 points each,

parts.text: Identify this process that Steven Pinker suggested is instinctual in a 1994 book. B.F. Skinner argued that it worked through a form of operant condition in his book Verbal Behavior.
acceptableAnswers: do not accept anything relating to learning an additional language

parts.text: Skinner's behaviorist arguments about language acquisition were savaged by this MIT linguist, the author of Syntactic Structures, who instead proposed that a "universal grammar" might be responsible.

Jerome Bruner attempted to explain oral language acquisition by developing scaffolding theory, which was based on this concept of Lev Vygotsky. This concept refers to the things a learner cannot do by themselves, but can do with guidance.

bonuses.leadin: The holophrastic and telegraphic stages occur during this process, the study of which is aided by a database founded by Catherine Snow and Brian MacWhinney. For 10 points each:

Tezcatlipoca was a rival of this primary deity of the Aztecs, a sun god known as the "plumed serpent."
One myth has Tezcatlipoca turning into this creature upon defeat by Quetzalcoatl; this spotted feline is the largest cat of Central America.

parts.text: Name these groups of three coequal Roman leaders, the second of which was comprised of Octavian, Marcus Lepidus, and Marc Antony.

After the death of Marcus Lepidus, the alliances of the Second Triumvirate were broken at the Battle of Actium, in which Octavian defeated the forces of Marc Antony and this Egyptian queen, his lover.
The First Triumvirate dissolved after the death of this "richest man in Rome" during a campaign against the Parthian Empire. Pompey and Julius Caesar went to war after his death.

bonuses.leadin: The Lex Titia officially installed one of these groups in 43 BCE. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this battle fought in 1993 that ended unsuccessfully with eighteen American soldiers dead and a much larger number of civilians dead or wounded.

The Battle of Mogadishu was fought in the capital of this country that has been in a state of civil war since 1991. Pirates have begun to use this African country and its coast as a base of operations.

Medals of Honor were awarded posthumously for defending the crew of Super Six Four to Gary Gordon and Randy Shughart, two members of this branch of the U.S. Joint Special Operations Command that focuses on counterterrorism and officially does not exist.

bonuses.leadin: This battle began as U.S. Army Special Forces closed in on warlord Muhammad Farrah Aidid during Operation Restore Hope. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this thinker who also analyzed Ahmad Safwat and Qasim Amin's efforts to reform colonial Egypt's legal system in Formations of the Secular.

This 1967 work by Peter Berger interprets religion as a "plausibility structure" that vanishes with secularization. Berger later retracted many of its claims, instead claiming the world was becoming "desecularized."
Jürgen Habermas wrote The Dialectics of Secularization along with this Catholic leader, who became the first pope emeritus in 600 years after resigning the papacy in 2013.

bonuses.leadin: A book by this thinker describes how Martin Luther King's language of Christian redemption was more successful than Malcolm X's idea of civil rights in permeating universalist conceptions of human rights. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name these chromosomes of which women have two and men one.
Highly condensed and inactivated x chromosomes are given this name. These entities are theorized to result in dosage compensation. Women who fail to develop these entities have Turner's syndrome.
Another sex determination system is the haplodiploid system, which is often used by this order of insects that contains wasps, bees, and ants.

bonuses.leadin: Lyon's hypothesis predicted the inactivation of these entities, and the coloration of calico cats is based on these chromosomes. For 10 points each:
